passage:
Crèche note, Friday

Alka, nineteen months, spent her first two days sitting by the door, not playing, not crying, just staring. Today I carried her on my hip while I set out snacks, and held her on my lap at story time. By noon she leaned her head on my shoulder. After lunch she crawled off to the blocks and laughed.
I will keep offering lap time. It is not spoiling.

Swati

qa.q: Where did Alka sit on her first two days?
qa.a: She sat by the door, not playing, just staring.

qa.q: How did Alka seem to feel in her first two days?
qa.a: She seemed withdrawn and unsure, missing comfort, so she only stared and did not play.

qa.q: What did Swati do that helped Alka settle?
qa.a: Swati carried Alka on a hip and held her during story time, giving warm closeness until she felt safe to play.

qa.q: How might Alka's parents feel reading this note?
qa.a: They would likely feel relieved and grateful that Alka is being comforted and starting to play.

grounding: It shows a toddler withdrawn when comfort is missing, and how being carried and held helps her feel safe and calm.

passage:
All day in the village, little Pallavi clung to Dadi's pallu and would not play. At dusk Amma came back from the fields, dusty and tired. Pallavi ran to her, arms up.
"Don't carry her so much, you'll spoil her," said Afreen from next door.
Amma lifted Pallavi anyway and sat on the charpai. "She just needs me," she said.
Pallavi tucked her face into Amma's neck. Soon she was humming, then sleeping.

qa.q: Where was Amma coming back from?
qa.a: Amma came back from the fields.

qa.q: How did Pallavi feel when Amma came home?
qa.a: She felt relieved and eager for closeness, running with her arms up and then settling into Amma's neck.

qa.q: Was Amma right to lift Pallavi, and why?
qa.a: Yes, because warm holding helped Pallavi calm down and fall asleep; it met a need rather than spoiling her.

qa.q: Why might Afreen worry about carrying Pallavi?
qa.a: Afreen may believe that too much carrying spoils a child, a common worry, even though Pallavi clearly needed comfort.

grounding: It shows a toddler who seeks to be held after a long day apart, and a mother who treats warm touch as a need, not spoiling.

passage: Since the new baby arrived in their Amman flat, two-year-old Jamal had turned clingy and whiny. He tugged at Rania's clothes all day, then sat alone by the window, sucking his thumb. Rania felt stretched thin. One morning she tied him to her back in the old sling while she stirred the lentils. Jamal rested his cheek against her shoulder and hummed. That evening he played happily with his blocks, and when the baby cried, he patted her gently.

qa.q: Where did Jamal sit alone?
qa.a: By the window.

qa.q: What was Jamal feeling since the new baby arrived?
qa.a: He felt left out and insecure, becoming clingy and then withdrawn.

qa.q: Why did carrying Jamal in the sling help?
qa.a: The closeness helped him feel safe and loved again, so he calmed and could play.

qa.q: How might Rania have felt with two small children needing her?
qa.a: She felt stretched thin and tired, trying to care for both.

grounding: Shows a toddler becoming clingy and withdrawn when comfort is missing, and warm closeness helping him feel calm and secure again.

passage:
Monday: Jyoti went back to work. When she came home, eighteen-month-old Jeevan didn't run to her. He turned his face away and played alone, quiet.
Wednesday: Jyoti sat on the floor after work and simply held him on her lap for twenty minutes, humming. He stiffened, then melted against her.
The next Monday: When the door opened, Jeevan ran shrieking to her, arms up, and nestled into her neck.

qa.q: What did Jeevan do when Jyoti came home on Monday?
qa.a: He turned his face away and played alone, quiet.

qa.q: How did Jeevan seem to feel on the first Monday?
qa.a: He seemed hurt and withdrawn after missing his mother all day.

qa.q: What did Jyoti do that rebuilt Jeevan's trust?
qa.a: She held him on her lap and hummed for twenty minutes after work.

qa.q: How might Jyoti have felt when he turned away on Monday?
qa.a: She was probably hurt and worried about returning to work.

grounding: Shows a toddler withdrawing when comfort is missing, and warm lap time helping him feel safe and trusting again.

passage: After daycare in their Bengaluru flat, two-year-old Sarika held up her arms to Jomon and wailed until he picked her up. She wanted carrying while he boiled the milk, while he fetched the clothes, everywhere. His aunt, visiting, frowned. 'You're spoiling her.' Jomon just shifted Sarika onto his hip. She tucked her head under his chin and stopped crying. After half an hour she wriggled down by herself and went off to play with her blocks, singing.

qa.q: Where did Sarika tuck her head?
qa.a: Under Jomon's chin.

qa.q: How did Sarika feel after daycare?
qa.a: She felt tired and needy, wailing to be picked up.

qa.q: Why was Jomon right to keep carrying her?
qa.a: Warm closeness helped Sarika feel safe, and once she felt calm she went off to play on her own.

qa.q: How might the aunt see Jomon carrying Sarika?
qa.a: She sees it as spoiling, not as comfort that helps a toddler settle.

grounding: Shows a toddler seeking to be carried after a long day, and warm touch helping her feel safe and calm rather than spoiling her.

passage:
"She's been crying since you left for the shop," Nani said, rocking Sangeeta on her hip.
Shalini dropped the bags. "Come, my baby."
Sangeeta flung out her arms and buried her face in Shalini's neck.
"You'll spoil her, always carrying," Nani said, smiling.
"She's been sick two days. She needs this."
Sangeeta's sobs slowed. Soon she was patting Shalini's cheek. "Amma. Mine."
"See? Calm now," Shalini said softly.

qa.q: Where had Shalini gone?
qa.a: She had left for the shop.

qa.q: How did Sangeeta feel when Shalini came back, and how can you tell?
qa.a: She felt relieved and safe; she flung out her arms, buried her face and her sobs slowed.

qa.q: Is Shalini spoiling Sangeeta by carrying her? Why or why not?
qa.a: No; warm holding after being sick helps a toddler calm down and trust that comfort will come.

qa.q: How does Nani see all the carrying?
qa.a: Nani teases that it spoils her, but she smiles, and she has been rocking Sangeeta on her hip too.

grounding: Shows a toddler seeking to be held for safety and calming quickly once comfort returns, with warm touch shown as care, not spoiling.
